title: AI Consulting in Practice – NLW, Superintelligent, @AIDailyBrief⁩
talk_summary: This is a market-research talk summarizing enterprise AI adoption surveys and a self-reported ROI study of ~2500 use cases, not a technical talk about agent engineering. It contains no mechanisms for building, routing, reviewing, or orchestrating agents—only aggregate statistics about where enterprises claim value.

takeaways.technique: Track ROI per use-case category to prioritize agent work
takeaways.what_they_do: They collect self-reported primary ROI benefit per use case across eight categories (time savings, output, quality, new capabilities, decisions, cost, revenue, risk) and compare distributions by org size and role.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the more use cases that a person or an organization submitted that the the better they tended to see uh ROI for
takeaways.numbers: ~2500 use cases; 44.3% modest ROI, 37.6% high ROI, ~5% negative; time savings ~35% of use cases

takeaways.technique: Breadth of use cases correlates with reported ROI
takeaways.what_they_do: They observe that organizations running more distinct AI use cases systematically report higher ROI than single spot experiments, and that agentic/automation use cases outperform.
takeaways.evidence_quote: where those use cases mention certain types of automation or they mention agents they wildly outperform in terms of the self-reported ROI
takeaways.numbers: Agent/automation use cases 'wildly outperform' (no figure given)
